title: Hand-rolled base64url encoding where Node's native `.toString('base64url')` exists
description: Two sites build base64url by hand: `buf.toString('base64').replace(/\+/g,'-').replace(/\//g,'_').replace(/=+$/,'')`. Node 16+ supports `buf.toString('base64url')` directly — a one-call, correct, standard replacement. customer-hash.ts is security-adjacent (PII pepper hash), so the clearer builtin is preferable. Genuine reinvention with an exact stdlib replacement.

title: Email-shape validation regex duplicated across ~11 route handlers
location: apps/main/src/app/api/**/route.ts (11 sites, e.g. groups/[id]/invitations/route.ts:100, admin/email-samples/route.ts:261, auth/microsoft-email-prompt/route.ts:80)
description: The same lightweight email check `/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/` (with a 254-char guard) is re-implemented in ~11 handlers. Functionally fine, but a consistency/maintainability indicator: one shared validator (or a Zod `.email()` schema, already a dependency) would remove the drift risk. Not a bug.
remediation: Extract a single `isValidEmail`/Zod email schema and call it from the 11 sites.

title: Manual currency formatting (`$${cents/100 .toFixed()}`) scattered across ~23 sites
description: 23 display sites format money by hand from cents. `Intl.NumberFormat('en-US',{style:'currency',currency:'USD'})` is the standard replacement and handles locale/negative/grouping correctly. Caveat verified in-code: several sites have BESPOKE rounding rules (e.g. `<$0.01` sentinel, variable decimal places) Intl does not do out of the box, so a blanket swap is wrong — these are partially-justified. Display-only, no correctness risk. Info tier.
remediation: Centralize into a `formatCents(cents, opts)` helper wrapping Intl.NumberFormat, preserving the intentional sentinel/rounding behavior; adopt where no bespoke rule applies.

title: M6 verdict summary: 52 indicators over real ATC code — maintainability/consistency signal, no correctness or security risk
description: First M6 reviewed verdict against a REAL target (clears the never-run-on-real-target gap). 52 hand-rolled indicators across 8 classes were triaged: GENUINE reinventions worth acting on — base64url (2, exact stdlib replacement), duplicated email regex (11, consolidate), scattered currency formatting (23, partial — bespoke rounding limits the swap). NON-ACTIONABLE / suppressed on review — cookie Set-Cookie header strings (8, idiomatic for Next.js route handlers), cookie parsing (3), random-string-id (3, all in test/e2e helpers), class-string merge (1), JSON deep-equal (1). Net: ~36 legitimate maintainability indicators, all Info/Low; the dominant theme is consistency (one email validator, one currency helper), not defects. No hand-rolled crypto/auth/tenancy primitive was found reinvented (the security-critical hand-rolled code — constant-time-equal, hmac-jwt, postgrest-filter escaping — was reviewed by the M1 core-isolation pass and judged sound).
